summary: Overlapping string transcode in a fused adapter can panic
description:
### Summary

Wasmtime contained a bug where components containing fused adapters, or components calling components, could trigger a panic on the host in some situations where a string is transferred from one location to another. Wasmtime historically raised a trap in this situation and recent refactorings meant that this trap was no longer raised.

### Impact

The impact of this bug is that a WebAssembly guest can trigger a `panic!()` in the host through normal default execution. This is considered a denial-of-service vector in Wasmtime. The precise scenario that a trap is raised is when a same-instance component-to-component call is made which transfers a string where the source and destination alias each other. Wasmtime prior to 49.0.0 raised a trap in this situation and refactorings in 49.0.0 meant that this no longer trapped but accidentally got the point of raising a panic. The precise behavior of this operation is something still being clarified in the upstream specification, and for now Wasmtime will continue to trap as it has historically done.

### Patches

Wasmtime 49.0.3 has been released fixing this issue and restoring the historical trap.
